question: The second five-year plan introduced to the concept of public sector of state-run enterprises based on the ____________ model of industrialisation.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Russian__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Second five-year plan was based on the Mahalanobis model, an economic development model developed by the Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1953.
 
• PC Mahalanobis established the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta in 1931 and for the same reason, he is known as the father of Indian Statistics. He was a member of the first Planning Commission of free India.
 
• The second five-year plan was for the year 1956-1961, this plan was based on the **Russian** model of industrialization.
 
• The second five-year plan focused on the development of the public sector and rapid Industrialisation. The plan attempted to determine a balanced allocation of investment between productive sectors in order to maximize long-run economic growth. 
 
• As a result, hydroelectric power projects across the country and five steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established with the help of Russia, Britain (the U.K), and West Germany respectively. Coal production was increased. More railway lines were added all over the country.
 
• The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and Atomic Energy Commission of India was established to promote research in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Basic information about planning commission and 5- year plans:

 
 
• Planning commission founded: 1950.
 
• Planning Commission head: Prime Minister
 
• First five-year plan launched: 1951
 
• A total number of 5- year plans: 12.
 
• Last five-year plan: 2012 to 2017.
 
• Planning Commission dissolved: 2014 (By PM Narendra Modi).
 
 

 
 

 Plan Year
 Highlight
 
 

 First Five-Year Plan (1951-56)
 
 
 
• It was presented by the first Indian Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru to the Parliament of India.
 
• This Plan was based on the Harrod Domar Model.
 
• Target growth was 2.1% and achieved growth was 3.6%.
 
 
 
 

 Second Five Year Plan (1956-61)
 
 
 
• The Second Five year Plan for rapid industrialization and the public sector.
 
• This model is called The Feldman–Mahalanobis model.
 
• The target growth rate was 4.5% and the growth rate was slightly less than expected, 4.27%.
 
 
 
 

 Third Five Year Plan (1961-66)
 
 
 
• The main focus was on Agriculture.
 
• Green Revolution initiated.
 
• The target growth rate was 5.6% but the actual growth rate was only 2.4%. 
 
 
 
 

 Fourth Five-Year Plan: (1969-74)
 
 
 
• This plan was also called the Gadgil Formula.
 
• The main focus of this plan was towards growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance.
 
• The target growth rate was 5.6% but the actual growth rate was 3.3%.
 
• 14 banks ware Nationalised.
 
 
 
 

 Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-78)
 
 
 
• Garibi Hatao slogan was raised.
 
• MNP was prepared by D.P.Dhar.
 
• The target growth rate was 4.4% but the actual growth rate was 4.8%.
 
 
 
 

 Rolling Plan
 1978-80
 
 

 Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-85)
 
 
 
• This was the beginning of the economic liberation by eliminating price controls.
 
• It was seen as the end of Nehruvian Socialism.
 
• Family planning was introduced to prevent over population.
 
• NABARD bank was established on the recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee in 1982.
 
• The target growth rate was 5.2% but the actual growth rate was 5.7%.
 
 
 
 

 Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-90)
 
 
 
• The main focus was on attaining self-reliance by 2000.
 
• The target growth rate was 5.0% but the actual growth rate was 6.01%.
 
 
 
 

 Annual Plan
 1990-92
 
 

 Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-97)
 
 
 
• This plan promoted the modernization of Industries.
 
• Panchayat and Municipality Act came.
 
• The target growth rate was 5.6% but the actual growth rate was 6.8%.
 
 
 
 

 Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002)
 
 
 
• It marks the fifty years of India's independence.
 
• Focus was on balanced relationship between rapid growth and the quality of life for people.
 
• The target growth rate was 7.1% but the actual growth rate was 6.8%.
 
 
 
 

 Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07)
 
 
 
• Te goal was to promote inclusive growth and equitable development.
 
• The target growth rate was 8.1% but the actual growth rate was 7.6%.
 
 
 
 

 Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-2012)
 
 
 
• C Rangarajan prepared the 11th plan.
 
• Main goal was rapid and more inclusive growth.
 
• The target growth rate was 9% but the actual growth rate was 8%
 
 
 
 

 Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17)
 
 
 
• This was the last five-year plan
 
• The goal was Faster, More inclusive and Sustainable Growth.
